1  W  to issue Writ of Mandamus, directing the Respondents herein to prov  alternative accommodation pertaining to the land acquisition procee  initiated by the Respondents comprised in Survey No. 241/7 to an ex  32 cents, situated at No. 121, Mugaiyur Village, East Coast Road, C  Taluk, the then Kancheepuram District presently Chengalpattu Distri  based on the petitioner's representation dated 10.04.2023, so as to  with the earlier order in W.P.No.10719 of 2019, dated 30.06.2021.
 For Petitioner : Mr.V.Ramanareddy  For Respondents : Mr.T.Arunkumar,
 Additional Government  ORDER

The relief sought in the present Writ Petition in W.P.No.16815 of 2023 is to direct the Respondents to provide alternative accommodation pertaining to the land acquisition proceedings initiated by the respondents comprised in Survey No. 241/7 to an extent of 32 cents, situated at No. 121, Mugaiyur Village, East Coast Road, Cheyyur Taluk, the then Kancheepuram District presently Chengalpattu District, based on the representation dated 10.04.2023 made by the petitiioner, so as to comply with t h e e a r l i e r o r d e r d a t e d 3 0 . 0 6 . 2 0 2 1 p a s s e d i n W . P . N o . 1 0 7 1 9 o f 2 0 1 9 .
https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis 2.
The learned counsel for the petitioner mainly contended that the land belonged to the petitioner was acquired for the expansion of East Coast Road projects.
Thus, the petitioner has submitted an application to provide alternative land enabling the petitioner to continue his activities.
Alternative accommodation cannot be claimed as an absolute right by filing a Writ Petition under Article 226 of the Constitution of India.

3. The scope of judicial review conferred under Article 226 of the Constitution of India cannot be expanded for the purpose of granting relief to provide alternative accommodation in the absence of establishing any right.

If any scheme is provided for such alternative accommodation, then alone the petitioner can claim it as a right, but not otherwise.
4.
Mere land acquisition would not confer any right to claim alternative accommodation, since the land losers are provided with compensation under the provisions of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894.
Therefore, in the absence of establishing any right to claim alternative accommodation, High Court will not issue any direction even to consider the representation.
By issuing a direction to consider the representation, the https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis litigants are back again to High Court and such directions would do no service to the cause of justice.

Mechanical issuance of such directions are paving wrong signal to public administration and there is a possibility of abuse of such order by the litigants and therefore, only in the event of establishing a right, High Court would be in a position to issue a direction and thus, the Writ Petition is not maintainable.

Accordingly, the Writ Petition in W.P.No.16815 of 2023 stands dismissed.
No costs.
